{"id":"PKIX-hz8g","title":"Documentation accuracy defects found in the prose cleanup","description":"Found while deslopping every hand-written doc in the workspace. These are
factual defects, not style, and each needs either a maintainer decision or
restructuring, so none was fixed in that pass. Fixed there and not listed
here: stale "planned" claims in AGENTS.md and pkix-aia/README.md, stale
counts in baseline-pkits-analysis.md, the pkix-lint oscal feature row, the
pkix-mta-sts "adapter does not exist yet" claim.

SECURITY-RELEVANT, HIGHEST VALUE

1. The SSRF destination policy drifts three ways across pkix-aia-http,
   pkix-net-guard and pkix-revocation-http.
   - The non-public address list is stated twice and inconsistently.
     pkix-aia-http says "loopback, private, link-local, ULA, multicast or
     unspecified". pkix-net-guard, which owns the policy, also covers RFC
     6598 shared space, 0.0.0.0/8, 240.0.0.0/4, IPv6 site-local, and the
     IPv4-mapped / IPv4-compatible / NAT64 forms — which it calls out as
     "the standard way an address filter is bypassed". A reader of
     pkix-aia-http alone would conclude ::ffff:127.0.0.1 is not covered.
   - pkix-revocation-http carries a prominent warning that it and
     pkix-aia-http "ship opposite defaults for the same threat. Do not
     carry an assumption from one to the other." pkix-aia-http's matching
     section says it "intentionally mirrors" that crate and never mentions
     the opposite default. The warning only works if both files carry it,
     and right now the crate with the safer default is the one without it.
   - pkix-net-guard says pkix-aia-http re-exports its resolvers;
     pkix-aia-http never names pkix-net-guard.

WRONG OR STALE CONTENT

2. pkix-revocation-http has a "## Planned API" section whose example does
   not match the shipped API: the trait is
   `fetch(&self, req: &FetchRequest<'_>) -> Result<FetchResponse, FetchError>`
   (src/lib.rs:441), not `fetch(&self, url: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>, _>`,
   and `HttpCrlFetcher::new` takes (fetcher, verifier, now_unix)
   (src/lib.rs:649), not two arguments. The crate is published at 0.3.0.
   The heading is currently the only thing warning a reader the snippet is
   not real, so fix the example first, then rename the heading.

3. pkix-truststore still lists pkix-truststore-system under "Placeholder
   adapter beads filed" with the scope "macOS Security framework, Windows
   CryptoAPI, iOS Keychain, Android KeyStore, Linux/BSD distro CA bundle
   paths". That crate shipped at 0.2.0 today. Needs the entry moved out of
   that list, which still legitimately holds PKCS#11, so the heading
   cannot just be relabelled.

4. pkix-truststore-system's rustdoc says "Keychain and CryptoAPI are
   feature-gated backends", but both are `#[cfg(target_os = ...)]` and its
   own Cargo.toml says "Declared per target rather than behind a feature".
   The README now says target-gated, which is the true version.

5. baseline-limbo-analysis.md: the PKIX-lwr9 follow-up bullet says the
   tc60 design call is still pending, while an earlier section says
   "PKIX-lwr9.4 / tc60 has been resolved by this work". One is stale and
   the pending bullet holds the only copy of the harness/API-gap
   diagnosis, so it needs reading rather than deleting.

6. baseline-pkits-analysis.md's per-bucket breakdowns were hand-classified
   against an earlier regeneration and their internal counts are from that
   run (the LooserThanWild table sums to 81 where the current total is
   62). The headings no longer claim counts and the file now says so, but
   the breakdowns want re-classifying against the current baseline.

DRIFTED DUPLICATES — pick a canonical version

7. The HSM/token vendor list differs between pkix-truststore ("YubiHSM,
   Thales, AWS CloudHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM, SafeNet, YubiKey PIV, smart
   cards, TPM 2.0 via tpm2-pkcs11, SoftHSM for testing") and
   pkix-truststore-pkcs11 ("Yubico HSM, ..., OpenSC-backed tokens, PIV /
   CAC smart cards, FIPS-mode deployments"). Drifted in spelling and
   membership: TPM 2.0 and SoftHSM in one only, OpenSC / CAC / FIPS-mode
   in the other.

8. pkix-lint-cabf and pkix-profiles-cabf share a ~90% identical CA/B Forum
   "not authoritative" preamble, but the snapshot sentence differs: "a
   snapshot of those requirements at the time of the most recent revision"
   versus "a small, curated snapshot of marquee BR requirements". One
   promises more completeness than the other for the same ballot-cycle
   problem.

9. pkix-chain's "what pkix-path validates" enumeration has drifted from
   pkix-path's own list, omitting trust-anchor matching and policy
   mappings. And pkix-chain's features table describes `crl` / `ocsp`
   differently from pkix-revocation's implementations table.

10. pkix-mta-sts and pkix-mta-sts-http justify the same PolicyStore /
    InMemoryPolicyStore fact differently ("survives the process but not a
    restart" versus "the workspace depends on no filesystem or OS").
    Both are good; they are out of sync.

11. AGENTS.md states the driving goal twice, differently: "RFC 5280 X.509
    for Rust, done right from the start" (Project phase) and "full RFC
    5280 and adjacent-RFC coverage" (Status). Quality framing versus
    scope, so possibly both are wanted — but possibly one is stale.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-11-26T07:22:16.308514126Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-11-26T07:22:16.308514126Z"}

{"notes":"Update after the rustdoc half of the pass finished.

NOW FIXED, so ignore these items above: item 4 (pkix-truststore-system's 'feature-gated backends' claim — corrected to per-target in both the README and the rustdoc, and the false 'No platform backend is enabled by default' line is gone). pkix-truststore's Source-coverage entries were also corrected, so item 3 is partly done: -system is no longer described as a skeleton, though the 'Placeholder adapter beads filed' list still needs restructuring since PKCS#11 genuinely belongs there.

ALSO FIXED during the rustdoc pass, for the record: a sentence left truncated mid-clause in pkix-aia ('...the variant uses the'); a malformed '## # Limitations' heading in pkix-aia-http; a stray blank line in pkix-profiles that split its doc block in two and orphaned a bullet; pkix-lint's claim that Warn/Error carry '&static str' when the type is Cow<'static, str>; pkix-difftest's claim that the OpenSSL and pyca oracles are stubbed and the pkits/pem-tree loaders are TODO, when all of PKIX-7nsf.1-.8 are closed and those modules are 400-odd lines each; stale 'planned' claims for pkix-aia/pkix-aia-http in pkix-path and pkix-path-builder; pkix-revocation's claim that its feature-gated checkers do network I/O (it opens no sockets) and that Ed25519/P-521/RSA-PSS are unimplemented gaps.

NEW, still open:

12. pkix-truststore says the only known panic mode is 'an upstream x509-cert
    0.2.x edge case (RustCrypto/formats#1965)... removed once the workspace
    bumps to x509-cert 0.3.x'. The workspace is on x509-cert 0.3 already
    (Cargo.toml:181), but the guard is still in from_pem (src/lib.rs ~511)
    with an inline comment making the same promise. Deleting the guard is a
    code change, so it was left.

13. pkix-identity's crate doc says 'Future trust-store adapters
    (pkix-truststore-system, pkix-truststore-pkcs11) use it to answer...'.
    Both crates exist, so 'future' is stale — but neither declares a
    pkix-identity dependency, so simply dropping the word makes it a false
    present-tense claim. Needs a decision about which is true.

14. pkix-chain/src/lib.rs:100 still carries the same stale algorithm-gap
    claim that was corrected in pkix-revocation (Ed25519 and RSA-PSS
    'tracked under PKIX-gphz').

15. pkix-aia-http's crate doc says 'No HTTP/2 connection pooling tuning
    beyond ureq::Agent's defaults'. The workspace pins ureq 3, which is
    HTTP/1.1 only, so the HTTP/2 framing is wrong rather than terse.

16. Lint-count disagreement: pkix-policy-zlint and pkix-zlint-bridge both
    say zlint's catalog is ~400 checks; pkix-profiles-cabf said ~700. The
    number was removed from pkix-profiles-cabf rather than picking a side.
    Neither figure was verified.

17. pkix-profiles says no_std + alloc support is 'planned for a future
    release' because ValidationPolicy 'holds owned Vec fields that
    currently require the standard allocator'. ValidationPolicy lives in
    pkix-path, which is no_std, so this looks doubtful.

STYLE CALL TO CONFIRM OR REVERT: the leading '# <crate-name>' heading was
removed from the crate docs of pkix-pkilint-bridge, pkix-policy-pkilint,
pkix-profiles-cabf, pkix-truststore-pkcs11 and pkix-truststore-system,
because rustdoc already renders the crate name as the page title and the
polished crates (pkix-path, pkix-rustls, pkix-truststore, pkix-tlsrpt,
pkix-net-guard, pkix-profiles, pkix-zlint-bridge) carry no such heading.
The workspace was split on it; this aligned the minority with the majority."}
